text:
Liam: ran into a weird onboarding surprise with the Go sampleapp: request IDs intermittently missing and debug spam when OTLP auto-instrumentation is enabled. Repro in containerized local dev.

Liam: Quick repro I used:
1) docker build -t sampleapp-go .
2) docker run -e REDWOOD_LOG_LEVEL=INFO -e OTEL_TRACES_EXPORTER=otlp sampleapp-go
3) curl -v localhost:8080/health && curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-test-abc' localhost:8080/api/predict multiple times (client retries on failure)

Liam: Logs (sanitized):
INFO  [req=hz2] incoming /api/predict
DEBUG [req=] http.RoundTripper got headers: map[Authorization:[Bearer sk-test-abc]]
INFO  [req=] responded 200

Aisha: Interesting — Go SDK instrumentation sometimes wraps net/http RoundTripper and can re-issue requests, losing context values attached to the original *http.Request. If our req-id lives in req.Context and the wrapper makes a new request without copying values, we lose it.

Marco: Also likely cause for DEBUG burst: some instrumentations call logrus.SetLevel(logrus.DebugLevel) on init when OTEL_* envs are set. If our logger snapshot happened before that, we'd see the flip.

Liam: Flipping import order (telemetry before logger) reduced repro frequency but didn't eliminate it.

Aisha: Two-pronged approach suggested:
- Change req-id attach point: set a property on *http.Request via a small wrapper that copies the context value onto request.Header (X-Redwood-Req) at middleware entry so downstream re-reqs retain the id.
- Make logger resilient: evaluate level lazily (on first log) or expose logger.Reconfigure() that telemetry can call after instrumentations initialize.

Marco: For redaction: the Go otel http instrumentation emits headers as http.Header (map[string][]string) which our redactor only handles for map[string]string. Add deep handling for map[string][]string and mask Authorization, Api-Key-like keys keeping last 6 chars. Also coerce byte slices if present.

Liam: Pushed a small repro branch with a stress script and sample Dockerfile showing the issue: https://git.internal/redwood/sampleapp-go/branch/otlp-import-race. Added a tiny harness that flips import order to demo differences.

telemetry-bot: Created ticket DX-7684: "Go sampleapp: otel import race causes req-id loss & redaction gap; logger level overridden". Linked branch, cc @devex.

Marco: Implementation plan: I'll update the redactor to handle map[string][]string + []byte cases and add unit tests. Aisha, can you prototype the HTTP wrapper to copy req-id into headers so reissued requests retain id?

Aisha: Yep, I'll prototype a middleware that sets r.Header.Set("X-Redwood-Req", reqID) at the earliest entrypoint and ensure the value is preferred when present for logging. Also will add a quick note to the onboarding README recommending telemetry.Register() before logger.Init() until we ship hooks.

Marco: For logger, proposed API: logger.Init(opts...) remains same but add logger.ReconfigureFromEnv() and logger.Init({Defer:true}). We'll call ReconfigureFromEnv() from telemetry.Register() so order doesn't matter. Also add explicit behavior doc: REDWOOD_LOG_LEVEL wins over OTEL_LOG_LEVEL when set.

Liam: That sounds good. For short-term, I'll add the README mitigation and a CLI warning if OTEL_* envs are set and REDWOOD_LOG_LEVEL is not.

telemetry-bot: DX-7684 updated: assignees Marco, Aisha; priority P2; status triage.

Aisha: I'll open a draft PR for the middleware and unit tests. Marco, please ping when the redactor branch is up and I'll validate with the repro harness.

Liam: Thanks team — will follow up once PRs land. :thumbsup:
